item.title: Dev Log 1: Introduction to Project Vertex
item.description:
Dearest Community,

Rustling Leaves Games was built on a vision, a dream where people can come together and build something beautiful. A group of like-minded individuals with full-time jobs, willing to pour sweat and tears into building a game that proves we are so much more than a number tossed to the side of a stack of papers on a recruiter’s desk or a name at the start of a gut-wrenching Human Resources layoff email. Our vision is a community-built game called Project Vertex.

item.title: Dev Log 2: Introduction the Trotson Radio
item.description:
Dearest Community,

We are so excited to announce the Trotson game mechanic, which will be featured in our upcoming game, Project Vertex. The Trotson radio is a handheld radio offering a variety of sounds from radio stations and mixtapes to let players rest their minds, sit back, and enjoy music. As you play the game, you will also discover mixtapes scattered across the world, each telling stories hidden behind powerful songs and even more powerful memories.

item.title: Dev Log 3: Sculpting Words: Narrative Design of Project Vertex
item.description:
Dearest Community,

Our narrative journey began with a short paragraph describing Project Vertex, lost within a 20-page Game Development Document (GDD). At the time, we only knew two things about Project Vertex: that it was a role-playing game where the players could affect the outcomes of the story, and that the story meant everything to the game. We wanted to make players laugh, be curious, and experience a sense of familiarity. What started as a paragraph has since turned into a document all of its own, called the Narrative Bible. This document outlines a breakdown of every episode, act, and scene within our game. Some things were easy to decide; nature showcases four seasons, so each episode is based on a new season. Acts are moments within the Episode. Scenes are the played-out scripts within the act itself. We quickly realized we were going to be overwhelmed with the sheer amount of work that it takes to write out a story. Without a story, you cannot create concept art; without concept art, there are no assets; without assets, you can’t whitebox game mechanics.

item.title: Dev Log 4: Words Into Art: The Concept Art Process
item.description:
Dearest Community,

How do we translate words into art? That is the age-old question we ask ourselves every day at Rustling Leaves Games!

Our concept art process begins with a character or environmental description; we call it a profile. The profile defines the character’s emotional tone, descriptive factors, and personality traits. That, coupled with the entire narrative design, allows us to create something truly amazing!

item.title: Dev Log 5: What’s in a Name: Choosing Our Game Title
item.description:
“The most expensive marketing mistake might happen before your game even has a logo.”
- Maria Amirkhanyan

Dearest Community,

Naming is one of the earliest product decisions devs encounter, yet it’s often based on brainstorming sessions and internal votes.

At Rustling Leaves Games, we’ve decided to treat it like any other product decision: define reasons, validate them with real-life players, and make the final choice using evidence rather than intuition. Of course we would have a biased opinion; we’re the ones making the game!
